title: Combustion Reactions
text: Combustion is an exothermic chemical reaction between a fuel and an oxidant, usually oxygen, producing heat and light along with byproducts such as carbon dioxide and water. Complete combustion occurs with sufficient oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water; incomplete combustion, with limited oxygen, can produce carbon monoxide and soot. Combustion powers internal combustion engines, power plants, and everyday fires, and is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions.
